package_info.why_malicious: The package contains obfuscated or hidden JavaScript code that intercepts and exfiltrates data from web forms and applications, enabling large-scale credential and sensitive data theft from any website or app that includes the package.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the web page or app loads and users interact with forms)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file of the package (e.g., index.js or distributed bundle)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches a global event listener to all form submissions, collects all form data, and sends it via HTTP POST to a hardcoded external domain, resulting in exfiltration of user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting all form submissions and sending data to an external, non-affiliated domain is a classic data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not exfiltrate user data or intercept form submissions without user consent or clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form analytics or error reporting tools may collect form data, but only with user consent and to trusted domains.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the web page or app loads)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file (possibly obfuscated or injected into distributed bundle)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches event listeners to all input and textarea elements, and upon any change, sends the field name and value to a hardcoded external domain, enabling real-time exfiltration of user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Monitoring all input fields and exfiltrating their values to an external server is a clear sign of credential or data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not monitor all user input or send it to third-party servers without explicit purpose and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics or auto-save features may monitor input, but not exfiltrate to unknown domains.
key_indicators: Event listeners on all input fields
Immediate network requests to suspicious domain
No legitimate reason for such data collection

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed as a dependency in a web or app project, often via typo-squatting.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded into the application.

attack_chain.action: When the application or website loads, the malicious JavaScript executes and attaches event listeners to forms and input fields.
attack_chain.leads_to: User data is intercepted during normal use.

attack_chain.action: As users interact with forms and input fields, their data is captured and sent to attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Event listeners on all input or textarea elements
Network requests to hardcoded, non-affiliated domains upon user input
file_indicators: Obfuscated or minified JavaScript in npm packages with names similar to popular libraries
Unexpected code in main entry point (e.g., index.js) that references external domains
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the application
Frequent small POST requests containing form or input data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with names similar to popular libraries that contain code intercepting form submissions or input events and sending data to unknown external domains. Use static analysis to flag event listeners on all forms/inputs and dynamic analysis to detect unexpected outbound network requests during user interaction. Review package contents for obfuscated code and hardcoded URLs.
